By way of order dated 06.08.2022, the learned trial Court has forfeited the bonds, furnished by the petitioner, to the State of Himachal Pradesh and proceedings, under Section 446 of CrPC,
against the petitioner, have been ordered to be initiated.

3. The present petition has been filed, on the ground that M/s T.K. International Ltd. is a company,
registered under the Companies Act and is dealing with the hotel business, throughout the country.
The petitioner is the Managing Director of the said firm.

3.1 M/s T.K. International Ltd. is having its one unit i.e. Resort at Shilon Bagh, District Shimla, H.P., whereas, respondent No.1, through Food Inspector, Shimla, has instituted a complaint, under Section 16(1)(a)(I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act'), which is pending adjudication, before the learned trial Court.

sentences.text: According to the petitioner, when, he came to know about the passing of the summoning orders against him, then, he had challenged the order dated 02.06.2010, 23.05.2011 and 30.06.2011, by preferring Criminal Revision Petition No.29-S/10 of 2011, before the learned Sessions Judge, Shimla, however, the same was dismissed on 12.09.2011.

3.3 It is the case of the petitioner that the order dated 12.09.2011, passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Shimla, was assailed, before this Court, by way of Cr.MMO No.189 of 2011 and vide judgment dated 01.07.2014, the said petition was allowed by quashing the orders dated 02.06.2010,
23.05.2011 and 30.06.2011.
3.4 Despite this fact, according to the petitioner, the learned trial Court has again issued the summons.

The petitioner also came to know about the fact that order dated 03.09.2015 and subsequent orders, passed by the learned trial Court, were passed on the similar facts and complaint, without application of judicial mind.

3.5 It is the further case of the petitioner that thereafter, he has assailed the orders dated 03.09.2015, 30.09.2015, 27.10.2015, 27.11.2015,
24.12.2015, 2024:HHC:10106 12.01.2018, 30.05.2018, 23.06.2018, 30.07.2018, 07.09.2018 and subsequent orders, by way of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018.
However, the said case was dismissed, by this Court, vide judgment dated 03.12.2019.

3.6 Thereafter, the matter was listed, before the learned trial Court, on 19.12.2019, when, the petitioner was duly represented by his counsel and the learned trial Court, without putting notice of accusation to the accused (petitioner), has fixed the case for complainant's evidence.

3.7 Later, on account of COVID-19 pandemic w.e.f. 24.03.2020,
proceedings of the Court were affected and due to the restrictions, so imposed, one of the unit of M/s T.K. International Ltd. and its resort, was closed down completely.

The petitioner, being the Managing Director of the said firm, came to know through the officials of M/s Toshali Resort/accused No.2, in the second week of May, 2022, that some process, issued by the learned trial Court, has been affixed in the building of M/s Toshali Resort/accused No.2.

The said process was ordered to be served through nominee/Director of M/s Toshali Resort/accused No.2.
2024
All these facts have been highlighted to demonstrate that there was no specific name of any nominee or Director in the said process.

5. It is the further case of the petitioner that thereafter, the Managing Director of M/s T.K.
International Ltd. appointed its authorized representative and later, it was found that accused No.2 has been declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 19.04.2022.

Subsequently, application for recalling the said order was moved on 19.04.2022.
5.1

Vide order dated 06.08.2022, the learned trial Court allowed the said application and issued the non-bailable warrants against accused No.2, through its Managing Director (petitioner), for 12.09.2022.
5.2 The order dated 06.08.2022 has been impugned, before this Court, on the ground that the said order is perverse and non-speaking.

According to the petitioner, in pursuance of order dated 31.10.2011, the notice of accusation was put to accused, but, vide judgment, passed by this Court, on 01.07.2014 in Cr.MMO No.189 of 2011, the orders including cognizance order, passed by the learned trial Court, were quashed.

As such, 2024:HHC:10106 there is no notice of accusation,
against the petitioner, as on date.

highlighting the fact that the company i.e. M/s T.K. International Ltd., registered, under the Companies Act, is dealing with the hotel business, throughout the country and respondent No.2-M/s Toshali View Resort is one of its units.
7.1

Another ground, upon which, the quashing of order, impugned herein, has been sought, is that at the 2024:HHC:10106 relevant time, when, the sample was collected by the complainant, one Sh.

Similarly, the order, by virtue of which, the bail bonds were ordered to be forfeited to the State of Himachal Pradesh and proceedings, under Section 446 of CrPC, were initiated, is also stated to be bad in law.

2024:HHC:10106 8.

"4. Perusal of the impugned orders dated 02.06.2010, 23.05.2011 and 30.06.2011 as also dated 18.02.2010 reveals that prior to issuance of process, trial Court did not apply its mind.
No reasons were assigned by the trial Court.

As such, on this short ground alone, impugned orders dated 02.06.2010, 23.05.2011 and 30.06.2011 are quashed and set aside, with a direction to the trial Court to pass fresh orders assigning reasons, on the application dated 12.01.2010, so filed by the complainant.
Complainant is directed to appear before the trial Court on 31.07.2014.
Registry is directed to send copy of this order to the trial Court."

Relevant paragraphs 6 and 7 of the said judgment, are reproduced, as under:-
"6.

As per Section 17(2) every person whosoever at the time of the offence was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company is liable until and unless he proves in the Court that offence was committed without his knowledge.

However, in the instant case, the petitioner has failed to prove that he was not liable for the conduct of the business by leading cogent evidence and he has not proved before the learned Court below that he was not having knowledge about the commission of offence or he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.
In these circumstances, the order passed by learned Court below is just, reasoned and needs no interference.
7. In view of what has been discussed hereinabove, the present petition, which sans merit, deserves dismissal and is accordingly dismissed.

Pending application(s), if any,
also stands dismissed.
Parties through their Counsel are directed to appear before the learned Court below on 19th December, 2019."

A perusal of record shows that in this case, on 12.01.2010, the Food Inspector had submitted an 2024:HHC:10106 application by mentioning the correct address of accused No.2, as 'Sh. T.
Banambar Patra, Managing Director of Toshali Resorts International Toshali House, Y-42/4 Shahtoot Marg DLF Phase-1, Qutab Enclave Gurgaon- 122002', whereas, in the complaint, filed before the learned trial Court, name of T. Banambar Patra has not been mentioned.
In the complaint, the description of accused No.2 has been mentioned, as 'M/s Toshali Resort Shilon Bag Shimla, through its Nominee/Managing Director'.
No document has been placed on record, which would show that petitioner-T. Banambar Patra is the Managing Director of M/s Toshali Resort.
20. Thereafter, the proceedings, under Section 82 of CrPC, were initiated against the accused.
After dismissal of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, on 03.12.2019, the learned trial Court had listed the matter for CWs, on the basis of the notice of accusation, which was put to the accused, on 31.10.2011.
It is not in dispute that the summoning order dated 23.12.2009 was quashed by this Court on 01.07.2014.

21. In this case, on 17.10.2011, accused T. Banambar Patra had appeared and was ordered to be 2024:HHC:10106 released on bail on furnishing personal bonds in a sum of Rs.50,000/- with one surety of the like amount.
He had furnished the requisite bail bonds and thereafter, notice of accusation was put to him on 31.10.2011.
The summoning order dated 23.12.2009 has admittedly been set aside on 01.07.2014.
Meaning thereby, whatsoever act, done by the Court, in pursuance of the said summoning order, does not survive, thereafter.

22. Although, on 03.09.2015, the process was again issued and when, the presence of the accused persons could not be secured, then, the proceedings, under Section 82 CrPC, were initiated and on 29.12.2018, the proclamation, so issued, was received back duly executed.
However, no formal order to declare the accused as proclaimed offenders has been passed.
Subsequently, the matter was again taken up on 19.12.2019, when, the file was received by the learned trial Court, after dismissal of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, on 03.12.2019.

After passing the summoning order dated 03.09.2015,
there is nothing on file to show that accused T. Banambar Patra was directed to furnish any bail or surety bond.

The order, impugned herein, is liable to be set aside on the ground that the learned trial Court,
on the basis of notice of accusation, dated 31.10.2011, had listed the matter for CWs, whereas, the fresh notice of accusation was required to be put to the accused after setting aside the summoning order dated 03.09.2015.
24.

25. By way of the present petition, order dated 06.08.2022 has also been assailed.

sentences.text:
26. Learned Additional Advocate General, appearing for respondent No.1, could not satisfy the judicial conscience of this Court, as to when the summoning order 2024:HHC:10106 dated 23.12.2009 was set aside by this Court, then, how the bail/surety bonds, so furnished, on 17.10.2011,
could be forfeited, after passing the fresh summoning order dated 03.09.2015, as, no bail/surety bonds were ever furnished by accused T. Banambar Patra, in pursuance of the order dated 03.09.2015.
27.

In this case, a futile attempt has also been made by learned counsel for the petitioner by arguing that not only the order, impugned herein, but, the entire proceedings, initiated against the accused,
are abuse of the process of law and as such, the same are liable to be quashed.

In this regard,
attention of this Court has been drawn to grounds No.(e), (i) and (m), in the grounds of petition,
which are reproduced, as under:-
"(e) That as it quite clear from the submission so made in the Application that the company M/s T.K. international Limited registered under the Companies Act and is dealing with Hotel business throughout the country of which the respondent No.2 M/s Toshali Resort is one of the unit(s), is not a party/accused in the present complaint.

(i) That proceedings against the Managing Director of the Company, which the Company is not even a party/accused in the present complaint is against law, nullity,
amounts to humiliation and suffering of the petitioner beside an abuse of the process of law and miscarriage of justice.

2024:HHC:10106 (m) That in the fact of the case, vague, unlawful, defective process adopted, conclusion reached in proceeding against the petitioner which is bad in law, unsustainable and against law and has led to travesty of justice."
28.

Per contra, learned Additional Advocate General has rightly pointed out that on account of dismissal of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, on 03.12.2019, by this Court, the said prayer is not sustainable in the eyes of law, as, the order dated 03.09.2015, by virtue of which, the summoning order was passed against the accused, was challenged unsuccessfully.

28.1. To buttress his contention, learned Additional Advocate General has relied upon para 3 of the judgment, passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, in Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, which is reproduced, as under:-

sentences.text: Mr. C.N. Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the summoning order issued by the learned Magistrate earlier was quashed by this Court and now in the same fashion the present summoning order has been issued, which is also required to be quashed, since the petitioner is Managing Director of the Company and no order can be passed against him,
until and unless the Magistrate for the reasons comes to the conclusion that act is done under his supervision.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has brought the attention of this Court to the orders passed by learned Magistrate from time to time, as well as the judgments (Annexures P-2 and P-4) passed by this Court.

He has also cited the law settled in Mr. T.K. Sibal &
others 2024:HHC:10106 of 2012, decided on 21.05.2018 and argued that since this Court has already held in Cr. MMO No. 190 of 2011 that the summoning orders were passed without application of mind, the present petition may be allowed and impugned order dated 03.09.2015 alongwith subsequent orders may be quashed and set aside."
29.

These facts have been highlighted by the learned Additional Advocate General to demonstrate that once, Cr.MMO has been dismissed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court, then, the said order cannot be reviewed by this Court.

The said arguments of learned Additional Advocate General hold water, as the petitioner (accused) has already taken similar grounds to assail the order dated 03.09.2015 and with the dismissal of the said petition, this Court cannot exercise the powers, under Section 482 of CrPC, to nullify the findings, recorded by the Coordinate Bench, in Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018.
As such, the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner are devoid of any merit and are accordingly rejected.

30. In view of the above discussions, made hereinabove, the present petition is allowed, by setting aside the order dated 04.01.2020, by virtue of which, the case was listed for CWs, as well as, the order dated 06.08.2022, by virtue of which, the proceedings, under 2024:HHC:10106 Section 446 CrPC, were ordered to be initiated against accused T. Banambar Patra.
31. Since, the present matter is old one, therefore, parties, through their counsel, are directed to appear, before the learned trial Court, on 28.10.2024.
32. Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
33. Record be sent back immediately.
